narrative:
The 2024 Cincinnati Reds opened the year with genuine electricity, riding a pair of Opening Weekend home runs from Will Benson and Christian Encarnacion-Strand to announce themselves as a team with real pop. Nick Martini's clutch double in the season opener set the tone for a scrappy, competitive club that believed in itself heading into April. Through the first month, the Reds played .519 ball, enough to keep the fanbase engaged and the playoff hopes alive.

May shattered the early optimism. The Reds went a dismal 9-18, their worst month of the season, and the high-leverage moments reflected the unraveling. Closer Alexis Díaz was torched twice in the span of a week — first surrendering a game-changing hit that let Arizona erase a lead, then getting burned by Shohei Ohtani in Los Angeles. Lucas Sims couldn't escape the fire either. The bullpen, which had looked like a strength entering the year, became the team's most glaring weakness as May turned into a month of slow-motion damage.

June and July represented the Reds at their most resilient. Spencer Steer's walk-off two-run homer on June 5th — the season's single most impactful positive play — ignited a stretch in which Cincinnati went 14-13 in June and 13-11 in July. Jeimer Candelario added a three-run blast in mid-June, and the lineup showed flashes of the ceiling this roster could reach. For a brief, hopeful moment, the Reds were playing like a team that could sneak into the wild card race.

August dismantled those dreams for good. The Reds went 12-17 as the bullpen continued to hemorrhage leads — Alexis Díaz surrendered a brutal two-run homer to Yasmani Grandal on August 25th in the season's most damaging single play, and Justin Wilson gave up multiple critical shots over the final weeks. Will Benson's massive three-run homer on August 28th briefly offered hope, but it was the exception in a month defined by squandered leads and missed opportunities. September brought modest recovery at 13-12, with Spencer Steer reaching 20 home runs and Elly De La Cruz punctuating the finale with a dazzling triple, but it all amounted to a 77-85 finish and another year watching October from home.

chapters.title: Opening Fireworks
chapters.description: The Reds burst out of the gate with big hits from new faces, building early confidence through a competitive March and April.

chapters.title: May Meltdown
chapters.description: A brutal 9-18 May exposed the bullpen's vulnerabilities as Alexis Díaz and Lucas Sims repeatedly surrendered critical leads.

chapters.title: Steer the Ship
chapters.description: Spencer Steer's walk-off homer ignited back-to-back winning months in June and July, briefly reigniting playoff dreams.

chapters.title: August Collapse
chapters.description: The bullpen's failures reached their peak as the Reds went 12-17, with crushing home runs allowed dooming any remaining postseason hopes.

chapters.title: Pride of September
chapters.description: With the playoffs out of reach, Steer hit his 20th homer and De La Cruz dazzled, giving fans reasons to believe in the future.
